clue.text: Greeting to welcome student for hard ski race

indicators.note: putting the student for the hard means one letter stands in place of the other in the greeting

parts.note: shalom is a Hebrew greeting meaning peace
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
L is a learner driver, a student, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: Someone says hello to a learner before a tough downhill race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to welcome' reads as the student being taken in, but the student replaces the H, which is what 'for hard' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A slalom is a downhill skiing contest weaving between poles, so it is a type of ski race.

clue.text: Balance railway building with works that are shelved?

definitions.text: building with works that are shelved?

parts.note: Libra is the zodiac sign of the scales or balance

explanation.surface: A building on a railway line that holds abandoned projects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelved' suggests postponed plans, but books are literally put on shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: A library is a building where books, literary works, are kept on shelves.

clue.text: Desert holiday

definitions.meaning: to desert is to abandon or go away from
a holiday is time off work, as soldiers get

explanation.surface: A trip to the Sahara.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave is to go away (desert), and leave as a noun is permitted time off (holiday).

clue.text: Old woman with new training routines for primates

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, one's old woman
drills are repeated training exercises

explanation.surface: A mother takes up fresh exercise regimes for apes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandrills are large West African monkeys with brightly coloured faces, so primates.

clue.text: Family from Aylesbury possibly getting a horse

indicators.note: family from a place puts the place name first, then the relatives

parts.note: Aylesbury is the county town of Buckinghamshire, abbreviated Bucks
kin are one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: A family from a Home Counties town acquires a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: BUCKS is Buckinghamshire, an English county northwest of London whose county town is Aylesbury.
explanation.definitionFit: A buckskin is a horse with a golden-tan coat and black mane and tail, named for the colour of deer hide.

clue.text: Brandy and Peanut, maybe, or another name given to goats?

definitions.meaning: brandy butter and peanut butter are both kinds of spread
goats ram with their heads, so whimsically they are things that butt

explanation.surface: Two pets, Brandy and Peanut, or perhaps goats, need another name.
explanation.walkthrough: Brandy and Peanut look like pet names; brandy butter is a British Christmas sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy butter and peanut butter are butters, and goats that headbutt are jokingly called butters.

clue.text: Language coach born south of India's capital

indicators.note: in a down clue south of means placed below, so the born letter comes after

parts.note: a coach is a railway carriage, a car

indicators.note: a word's capital is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A tour coach comes into being in southern India.
explanation.definitionFit: Carib is the language of the Carib people of the Caribbean coast of South America.

clue.text: Icy Kent's dreadful day that brings disaster

indicators.note: dreadful signals that the letters are in a terrible state, so rearranged

explanation.surface: An awful freezing day in Kent ends in calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in southeast England.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky end is an unpleasant death or downfall, a personal disaster.

clue.text: Naive girl in grand location going topless

parts.note: taken as written
G is short for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: topless means losing its top, the first letter in a down light

parts.note: a venue is a location for an event

explanation.surface: An innocent young woman at a smart venue takes her top off.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingénue is an innocent, unsophisticated young woman, especially as a stock stage role.

clue.text: Mind keeping minutes internally for intensive group discussion?

parts.note: the brain is the mind

indicators.note: internally says the minutes go inside the word for keeping

parts.note: storing means keeping

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take care of the minutes of a meeting themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mind' looks like an instruction to look after the minutes, but it is a noun giving BRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainstorming is a session where a group throws out ideas rapidly; the question mark flags the loose description.

clue.text: Spooner's interpretation of good-looking Native American as happy-go-lucky

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds of the two words change places

parts.note: fair means good-looking, as in a fair maiden
the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A cleric's garbled description of a handsome Native American as carefree.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of FAIR CREE gives CARE FREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree and happy-go-lucky are synonyms, both describing someone untroubled by worry.

clue.text: Extremely hot theme in Hollywood TV shows

definitions.meaning: extremely hot weather is described as scorching
Paul Hollywood judges The Great British Bake Off, so the subject of his shows is cake-making

explanation.surface: The subject of glamorous Los Angeles television is sizzling.
explanation.walkthrough: Hollywood is not Los Angeles but Paul Hollywood, judge on The Great British Bake Off, a British TV home-cooking contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Baking means very hot as an adjective, and it is also the craft of making bread and cakes.

clue.text: Token lump by my shoulder's beginning to recede

indicators.note: receding means going back, so the assembled letters are read backwards

parts.note: lob is a dialect word for a lump

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone notices a swelling near their shoulder starting to go down.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol is a token: something that stands for or represents something else.

clue.text: Sad fib one treated in good faith

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A miserable little lie handled in good faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Bona fides is Latin for good faith, meaning honest intent or genuine credentials.

clue.text: Doctor refused to accept female endured pain

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the female letter goes inside the rearranged word
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor declined to see a woman who was in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician but is the anagram signal; SUFERED (from 'refused') takes in F.
explanation.definitionFit: To have suffered is to have endured pain, the plain meaning of the verb.

clue.text: Distance across river daughter works out immediately

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river

indicators.note: works out means makes its way out, so the daughter's letter leaves

parts.note: width is the distance across something, side to side

explanation.surface: Measuring the span of a river, a daughter calculates it at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works out' looks like solving a sum but means D leaves WIDTH, leaving WITH.
explanation.definitionFit: Forthwith is a formal adverb meaning at once, without delay.

clue.text: Worried song idea needs new arrangement

indicators.note: a song given a new arrangement has its parts reordered, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A songwriter frets that a tune concept needs reworking.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonised means anguished or fretting, a strong form of being worried.

clue.text: Decorate rear of mansion having vulgar exterior

indicators.note: exterior says the word for vulgar sits outside the picked letter

parts.note: garish means gaudy or vulgar

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Tarting up the back of a house that has a tasteless outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To garnish is to decorate, as with food or trimmings.

clue.text: Entire media, on reflection, admitting fault

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
admitting means letting in, so the two words hold the letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The press as a whole, after thinking, owns up to a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read 'admitting fault' as the definition, but that left the hidden letters with no signal: 'admitting' is the containment indicator and 'fault' alone defines. 'on reflection' reads the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A demerit is a mark against someone for wrongdoing, a failing or flaw.

clue.text: Cut down on consuming mead with lunch regularly

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the picked letters go inside the word for on

parts.note: re means on, concerning

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter is taken from the words

explanation.surface: Advice to drink less mead with your midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' looks like drinking the mead, but it is the containment signal; 'regularly' acts on 'mead' and 'lunch' separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce is to cut down, making something smaller or less.

clue.text: Have something to do with business

definitions.meaning: to involve or relate to something
a business is a firm or company

explanation.surface: Dealing with a commercial firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Concern as a verb means to relate to or involve, and as a noun a business firm, as in a going concern.

clue.text: Favour from a boxing judge

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds a head
ref, short for referee, is a judge in sport

explanation.surface: Getting a favourable decision from a boxing official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing judge' suggests a boxing referee, but 'boxing' is the containment signal; 'a' means each, as in a pound a head.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefer something is to favour it over the alternatives.

clue.text: Now and again arrest crook, old-fashioned in style

indicators.note: now and again says only every other letter of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Police sometimes nab a criminal who dresses in a dated way.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes a style deliberately imitating fashions of the recent past.

clue.text: Various traps through an oddly abandoned wood

indicators.note: traps means holds within, so the picked letters sit inside the word for various

parts.note: many means various, several

indicators.note: abandoning the odd letters leaves the even ones of the words

explanation.surface: Assorted snares set in a wood that has been deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters of 'through an' leaves HOGA, trapped in MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a reddish-brown tropical hardwood used for furniture.

clue.text: Audibly horses chomp on pasture

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word for horses is spoken

parts.note: greys are grey horses

explanation.surface: You can hear the horses munching in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: To graze is to eat growing grass in a field, as livestock do.

clue.text: Uncertain having organised teatime and dinner

indicators.note: letters that are organised are put into order, so the two words are rearranged together

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure, having arranged both an afternoon tea and an evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeterminate means not fixed or settled, so uncertain.

clue.text: Gradually stop aggressive move by Captain Kirk perhaps, ignoring resistance

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so a letter is dropped

parts.words: aggressive move by Captain Kirk perhaps
parts.note: Captain Kirk of Star Trek draws his phaser, a ray gun, when things turn hostile: phaser out
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A starship captain gradually calls off hostilities, not meeting any opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: A phaser is the ray gun of Star Trek; drop R from PHASER OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To phase something out is to withdraw it in stages, so to stop it gradually.

clue.text: Selfish individual employs a German for gardening work

indicators.note: employs here means takes in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a hog is a greedy, selfish person
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A self-centred person hires a German to do the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoeing is breaking up soil and weeding with a hoe, a garden chore.
